name: form-builder
purpose: A form designer that produces the schema and UI schema Schema Form renders. A palette of field types (click, Enter, or pointer drag onto the canvas), a canvas whose fields reorder by pointer drag or keyboard (Sortable List), a properties panel for label, name, required, validation, options, help text, width, and visibility conditions, a live Schema Form preview, a JSON view with validated import, and undo/redo. Emits aui-change with { schema, uiSchema } after every valid edit.
whenToUse: Administrators define forms (questionnaires, request types, intake forms) without a release.
Prototyping a form and handing the JSON to developers.
whenNotToUse: End users filling in forms: render them with Schema Form.
Nested or computed form logic beyond the supported conditions: edit the JSON or write the form by hand.
responsive: Palette, canvas, and properties sit side by side when the builder is at least 56rem wide (container query) and stack in one column otherwise.
rtl: Logical properties throughout; the three panes mirror and Sortable List handles RTL reordering.
theme: Global tokens only; the selected field uses color-selected and color-selected-text, the drop line color-primary; forced colors use Highlight.
timezone: Not applicable to the builder; date fields it creates behave as described for Schema Form (the working-days switch sets disableNonWorking).
security: Every label, option, and help text is rendered as text. Imported JSON is parsed with safeJsonParse (1 MB limit) and validated against the supported subset before it is applied; conditions are data, never code.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry: the host stores the emitted document.

performance.testedScale: Up to 200 fields on the canvas; 100 undo steps stored as JSON Patches.

limitations: The builder edits top-level fields; nested groups and lists from imported JSON are kept and can be reordered, renamed, and removed, but their inner fields are edited in the JSON view.
The visibility editor writes one condition per field (equals, does not equal, is filled, is empty); combined conditions are kept and edited in the JSON view.
unsupported: Custom field types in the palette.
antiPatterns: Letting end users edit the schema of a form they are filling in.
